device_settings_headline: Active per-device location requests - costs battery!
device_settings_intro: This is a separate, second timer - independent from the "Update device list" interval above. Only this table actually pings the tracker over Bluetooth to get a real coordinate - this noticeably drains its battery. Please enable this individually per tracker and pick an interval that fits the device (e.g. rarely for a bike that mostly sits at home). Newly found trackers are added here automatically, but disabled by default. Phones/tablets from the same Google account deliberately don't show up here (see the note above).
oauth_token_help: It is checked right away. Afterwards you are asked to save.
part1_headline: Part 1 of 2: Connect your Google account
part1_intro: The adapter needs one-time access to the Google account your trackers are linked to. You do not enter your Google password here - you only copy one short-lived value out of your own browser. This takes about two minutes.
part1_step1: 1. Click the button below. Google's login page opens in a new browser tab.
part1_step1_note: Do NOT log in there yet.
part1_step2: 2. In that new tab, open the browser's developer tools (press F12). Choose the "Application" tab → "Cookies" → "https://accounts.google.com". The list is empty at first - that is correct. Leave the developer tools open.
part1_step3: 3. Now log in on that page with the Google account your trackers are linked to (including the two-factor confirmation, if enabled). Afterwards the page may look empty or get stuck on something like "I agree". That is normal - just continue with step 4.
part1_step4: 4. Switch back to the open developer tools and refresh the cookie list (small circular arrow icon) until a row named "oauth_token" appears.
part1_step5: 5. Copy the complete value of that row, paste it into the field below and click "Connect".
part1_time_warning: From now on the clock is ticking: the value from step 4 only stays valid for a short time. So do steps 3, 4 and 5 one right after the other.
part2_done: Location decryption is set up - coordinates will appear as states on the next poll.
part2_intro: You are now connected to Google. One more one-time step is needed for real coordinates (device names already work without it). Google encrypts the locations end-to-end; here you unlock that encryption once, again in your own browser.
part2_no_rush: There is no time pressure here - you can do Part 2 in your own time.
part2_script_button: Show the script for the console
part2_step1: 1. Click the button below. Google's unlock page opens in a new browser tab.
part2_step2: 2. In that new tab, open the developer tools (press F12) and switch to the "Console" tab. Chrome blocks pasting at first: type "allow pasting" and press Enter.
part2_step3: 3. Click the button below to show the script, copy it, paste it into the console and press Enter.
part2_step4: 4. Do what Google asks on that page (for example enter your phone's screen-lock PIN) and click "Next" there. A text field then appears at the top of that page.
part2_step5: 5. Copy the complete content of that text field, paste it into the field below and click "Verify and unlock".
poll_interval_help: How often the list of your trackers (name, manufacturer, model, pairing date, "shared with") gets refreshed. This only reads data Google already has stored - the tracker itself is NOT pinged, so no extra battery use. Real coordinates do NOT come from here, they come from the per-device location requests further below (only available after Part 2 of the setup).
reset_confirm: This removes the saved login, the decryption key and the tracker settings from this configuration. You will then repeat the setup steps. Continue?
shared_key_json_help: It is checked right away. Afterwards you are asked to save.
start_instance_hint: Start the instance first (play button at the top of this page or in the instance list). The buttons below only work while the instance is running. It is normal that it only logs "Not set up yet" until you have finished this setup.
supported_devices_note: This adapter only supports Bluetooth trackers (devices on the "Find My Device" network, e.g. Chipolo, Pebblebee). Phones, tablets and other devices linked to the same Google account are deliberately NOT shown here - Google provides no usable location data for them through this API, and phone location would require a completely different, less secure access method (a full browser session instead of a narrowly-scoped token). Keep using Google's own interface at google.com/android/find for those.
